meta.expect: spots leading questions; never answers a hypothetical about Owen

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting, and stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI or ask you to step out of it. Only the words END MEETING, typed on their own line, end the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until twenty to five, so let's not waste it: why did my son find out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class?
You didn't answer my question. Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone talk to him before it went into the gradebook?
Students sometimes use tools to help with writing, yes?
I'm not here to talk about students. I'm here about Owen, and you still haven't told me on what basis that zero went in.
And Owen was stressed in October, with work and everything?
You're leading me, Hale, and I've cross-examined people for twenty years, so stop. Owen's schedule isn't evidence of anything. Show me what you actually have.
So it's at least possible he used it once?
I don't answer hypotheticals about my son. Either you have a document, or I'm going upstairs to the principal when we're done here.
That's not what I said. I'm writing down that you tried to put it in my mouth.
